lessons.title: Quoting Text Evidence, Inferences & Theme
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Quoting Evidence & Finding Theme
lessons.reading: Strong readers quote exact details from a passage to prove an inference. The theme of a story is its central life lesson—what the characters learn through challenges and choices.

principles.title: Text Evidence, Inferences, and Theme
principles.summary: Quote accurately from a text to support inferences and determine theme.

bank.passage: Maya practiced her violin for twenty minutes every evening, even when the notes sounded squeaky. By the spring concert, she played her solo smoothly.
bank.prompt: What is the theme of this passage?
choices: Violins are too hard to play
bank.explanation: Theme is the life lesson of a story; Maya’s daily effort helped her succeed.

bank.passage: Leo noticed the new student sitting alone at lunch. Leo walked over, smiled, and asked, "Want to join our table?"
bank.prompt: Which trait best describes Leo based on the text?
bank.explanation: Text evidence shows Leo kindly invited a lonely student to sit with him.

bank.passage: The heavy rain flooded the trail. Eli checked his map and led his sister along the high ridge so their boots stayed dry.
bank.prompt: Which detail proves Eli is a careful problem solver?
choices: He checked his map and took high ground
It rained heavily on the trail
bank.answer: He checked his map and took high ground
bank.explanation: Strong text evidence directly supports the claim with specific actions from the passage.

bank.prompt: What is an inference when reading a story?
choices: A conclusion based on text clues and experience
The title printed on the cover
bank.answer: A conclusion based on text clues and experience
bank.explanation: An inference combines details in the text with what you already know to figure out unstated ideas.

bank.passage: Cara wanted to ride the tall roller coaster, while her brother Ben preferred the calm ferris wheel. They agreed to ride one together first.
bank.prompt: How do Cara and Ben differ in this story?
choices: Cara likes fast thrills; Ben likes calm rides
bank.answer: Cara likes fast thrills; Ben likes calm rides
bank.explanation: Comparing characters shows how their feelings or choices are alike and different.

bank.prompt: Why do readers use quotation marks when citing text evidence?
choices: To show the exact words from the author
bank.answer: To show the exact words from the author
bank.explanation: Quotation marks enclose a direct quote copied word-for-word from the text.

bank.passage: When the team lost the final game, Captain Sam shook every player’s hand and said, "We played hard and learned a lot today."
bank.prompt: What theme does Sam’s response show?
choices: Good sportsmanship matters win or lose
Winning is the only thing that counts
bank.answer: Good sportsmanship matters win or lose
bank.explanation: Sam’s encouraging words after a loss show the lesson of good sportsmanship.

bank.passage: Mira stared at her empty bird feeder. Tiny footprints in the snow led straight to a plump squirrel under the pine tree.
bank.prompt: What can the reader infer happened to the birdseed?
choices: The wind blew the feeder away
Mira forgot to buy a feeder
bank.explanation: The empty feeder and footprints leading to a plump squirrel are clues that support this inference.

lessons.title: Main Idea, Text Structure & Author’s Evidence
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Informational Text Structures & Evidence
lessons.reading: Informational texts organize ideas using structures such as cause/effect, compare/contrast, problem/solution, or sequence. Authors support their main claims with facts, statistics, and examples.

principles.title: Main Idea, Text Structure, and Supporting Evidence
principles.summary: Identify main ideas, informational text structures, and supporting evidence.

bank.passage: Honeybees pollinate apple, almond, and berry crops. They also make honey and beeswax. Because of their work, farms grow far more food.
bank.prompt: What is the main idea of this passage?
choices: Honeybees are helpful insects that support food crops
bank.answer: Honeybees are helpful insects that support food crops
bank.explanation: The main idea is the central point that all supporting details in the paragraph explain.

bank.passage: Because heavy snow blocked the mountain pass, road crews closed the highway for six hours until snowplows cleared the lanes.
bank.prompt: Which text structure does this passage use?
bank.explanation: Cause and effect explains why something happened (heavy snow) and what resulted (road closure).

bank.passage: Both frogs and toads are amphibians. However, frogs have smooth, wet skin and long jumping legs, while toads have dry, bumpy skin.
bank.prompt: How is the information in this passage organized?
bank.explanation: Compare and contrast shows how two topics (frogs and toads) are alike and different.

bank.passage: Plastic bottles litter city parks. To solve this problem, the town installed recycling bins and refillable water stations near every playground.
bank.prompt: Which text structure does the author use here?
bank.explanation: Problem and solution states an issue (litter) and explains actions taken to fix it.

bank.passage: First, gather two slices of bread and peanut butter. Next, spread peanut butter on one slice. Finally, press the slices together.
bank.prompt: Which text structure is used in this passage?
bank.explanation: Signal words like "First," "Next," and "Finally" show steps in sequence order.

bank.passage: Wearing a bike helmet protects your head. Studies show helmets reduce serious head injuries by more than half during falls.
bank.prompt: What evidence supports the author’s claim about bike helmets?
choices: Studies show helmets cut head injuries in half
bank.answer: Studies show helmets cut head injuries in half
bank.explanation: Authors use facts and study results as evidence to prove their claim is true.

bank.prompt: Which signal words often show a compare-and-contrast text structure?
choices: Both, similarly, however, on the other hand
bank.answer: Both, similarly, however, on the other hand
bank.explanation: Words like "both" and "however" signal similarities and differences between two subjects.

bank.prompt: What should a good summary of an informational article include?
choices: The main idea and key supporting details
Every single word from the article
Only the last word of the page
bank.answer: The main idea and key supporting details
bank.explanation: A summary briefly states the main idea and the most important details in your own words.

units.title: Unit 2: Figurative Language, Word Roots & Grammar

lessons.title: Similes, Metaphors, Personification & Idioms
lessons.reading: Similes compare two things using "like" or "as." Metaphors compare directly without "like" or "as." Personification gives human actions to non-human things, and idioms/adages carry non-literal meanings.

principles.title: Figurative Language, Idioms, and Adages
principles.summary: Interpret similes, metaphors, personification, idioms, and proverbs.

bank.prompt: What type of figurative language is "The lake was a shining mirror"?
bank.explanation: A metaphor compares two things directly without using "like" or "as."

bank.prompt: What type of figurative language is "Her hands were as cold as ice"?
bank.explanation: A simile compares two things using the word "like" or "as."

bank.prompt: What does the idiom "spill the beans" mean?
bank.explanation: An idiom is an expression whose figurative meaning differs from the literal words.

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses personification?
choices: The autumn wind whispered through the trees.
The wind blew at ten miles per hour.
The tree is forty feet tall.
bank.answer: The autumn wind whispered through the trees.
bank.explanation: Personification gives human actions or feelings (like whispering) to non-human things.

bank.prompt: What does the adage "Actions speak louder than words" mean?
choices: Your actions matter more than your words
Shouting is the best way to talk
bank.answer: Your actions matter more than your words
bank.explanation: An adage or proverb is a traditional saying that shares a common truth or piece of advice.

bank.prompt: What does the idiom "under the weather" mean?
bank.explanation: The idiom "under the weather" means feeling unwell.

bank.prompt: What does the metaphor "The classroom was a beehive of activity" mean?
bank.explanation: Comparing the classroom to a beehive shows that everyone was actively working.

bank.prompt: Which sentence contains a simile?
choices: The kitten crept like a shadow across the rug.
The kitten is a tiny tiger.
The rug was soft and warm.
bank.answer: The kitten crept like a shadow across the rug.
bank.explanation: Using "like" to compare the kitten to a shadow makes this a simile.

lessons.title: Greek & Latin Roots, Prefixes & Context Clues
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Greek & Latin Roots and Affixes
lessons.reading: Common Greek and Latin roots unlock unfamiliar words: tele (far), photo (light), bio (life), port (carry), and spect (look). Combine root meanings with prefixes like pre- (before) and suffixes like -less (without).

principles.title: Greek/Latin Roots, Affixes, and Context Clues
principles.summary: Use Greek and Latin roots, prefixes, suffixes, and context clues to define words.

bank.prompt: What does the Greek root "tele" (as in telescope) mean?
bank.explanation: The Greek root "tele" means far away, so a telescope helps you see distant stars.

bank.prompt: What does the Latin root "port" (as in transport) mean?
bank.explanation: The Latin root "port" means to carry; "transport" means to carry across from one place to another.

bank.prompt: What does the Greek root "photo" (as in photograph) mean?
bank.explanation: The Greek root "photo" means light, used in words like photograph and photosynthesis.

bank.prompt: What does the prefix "pre-" mean in the word "preview"?
bank.explanation: The prefix "pre-" means before, so "preview" means to view beforehand.

bank.prompt: What does the suffix "-less" mean in the word "fearless"?
bank.explanation: The suffix "-less" means without, so "fearless" means without fear.

bank.prompt: What does the Greek root "bio" (as in biology) mean?
bank.explanation: The Greek root "bio" means life; biology is the study of living things.

bank.prompt: What does the Latin root "spect" (as in inspect) mean?
bank.explanation: The Latin root "spect" means to look; to inspect means to look closely at something.

bank.prompt: The arid desert had no rain. What does "arid" mean?
bank.explanation: The context clue "no rain" tells the reader that "arid" means very dry.

lessons.title: Perfect Verb Tenses, Conjunctions & Titles
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Perfect Verb Tenses & Conjunctions
lessons.reading: Perfect verb tenses use has/have/had + a past participle (e.g., "She has finished"). Correlative conjunctions work in pairs (either/or, neither/nor). Italicize book titles and put short story or poem titles in quotation marks.

principles.title: Verb Tenses, Conjunctions, Commas, and Titles
principles.summary: Use perfect verb tenses, correlative conjunctions, introductory commas, and title formatting.

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses the present perfect verb tense correctly?
choices: She has finished her science project.
She will finish her project tomorrow.
bank.answer: She has finished her science project.
bank.explanation: Present perfect tense uses "has" or "have" plus a past participle (has finished).

bank.prompt: Which pair of words is a correlative conjunction?
bank.explanation: Correlative conjunctions work in pairs, such as "either/or," "neither/nor," and "both/and."

bank.prompt: Choose the correct word: "Neither the coach ___ the players were late."
bank.explanation: "Neither" always pairs with the correlative conjunction "nor."

bank.prompt: Where does a comma belong in "Yes I would love to help"?
bank.explanation: Use a comma to set off introductory words like "Yes," "No," or "Well" at the start of a sentence.

bank.prompt: How should the title of a full-length book be formatted?
bank.explanation: Titles of long works like books, movies, and newspapers are italicized or underlined.

bank.prompt: How should the title of a short poem or short story be punctuated?
bank.explanation: Use quotation marks around titles of short works like poems, articles, songs, and short stories.

bank.prompt: Which sentence has an inappropriate shift in verb tense?
choices: Sam walked to the door and opens it.
Sam walked to the door and opened it.
Sam walks to the door and opens it.
Sam will walk to the door and open it.
bank.answer: Sam walked to the door and opens it.
bank.explanation: Verbs describing actions at the same time should stay in the same tense (walked / opened).

bank.prompt: What part of speech is "Wait!" in "Wait! Watch out!"?
bank.explanation: An interjection is a word or phrase that expresses strong or sudden emotion.

lessons.reading: Complete the Unit 2 Exam on similes, metaphors, idioms, Greek and Latin roots, verb tenses, conjunctions, and punctuation.

principles.title: Figurative Language, Idioms, and Adages
principles.summary: Identify and explain similes, metaphors, idioms, and adages.

bank.prompt: What type of figurative language is "The lake was a shining mirror"?
bank.explanation: A metaphor compares two things directly without using "like" or "as."

bank.prompt: What type of figurative language is "Her hands were as cold as ice"?
bank.explanation: A simile compares two things using the word "like" or "as."

bank.prompt: What does the idiom "spill the beans" mean?
bank.explanation: An idiom is an expression whose figurative meaning differs from the literal words.

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses personification?
choices: The autumn wind whispered through the trees.
The wind blew at ten miles per hour.
The tree is forty feet tall.
bank.answer: The autumn wind whispered through the trees.
bank.explanation: Personification gives human actions or feelings (like whispering) to non-human things.

bank.prompt: What does the adage "Actions speak louder than words" mean?
choices: Your actions matter more than your words
Shouting is the best way to talk
bank.answer: Your actions matter more than your words
bank.explanation: An adage or proverb is a traditional saying that shares a common truth or piece of advice.

bank.prompt: What does the idiom "under the weather" mean?
bank.explanation: The idiom "under the weather" means feeling unwell.

bank.prompt: What does the metaphor "The classroom was a beehive of activity" mean?
bank.explanation: Comparing the classroom to a beehive shows that everyone was actively working.

bank.prompt: Which sentence contains a simile?
choices: The kitten crept like a shadow across the rug.
The kitten is a tiny tiger.
The rug was soft and warm.
bank.answer: The kitten crept like a shadow across the rug.
bank.explanation: Using "like" to compare the kitten to a shadow makes this a simile.

principles.title: Greek/Latin Roots, Affixes, and Context Clues
principles.summary: Decode words using roots, prefixes, suffixes, and context.

bank.prompt: What does the Greek root "tele" (as in telescope) mean?
bank.explanation: The Greek root "tele" means far away, so a telescope helps you see distant stars.

bank.prompt: What does the Latin root "port" (as in transport) mean?
bank.explanation: The Latin root "port" means to carry; "transport" means to carry across from one place to another.

bank.prompt: What does the Greek root "photo" (as in photograph) mean?
bank.explanation: The Greek root "photo" means light, used in words like photograph and photosynthesis.

bank.prompt: What does the prefix "pre-" mean in the word "preview"?
bank.explanation: The prefix "pre-" means before, so "preview" means to view beforehand.

bank.prompt: What does the suffix "-less" mean in the word "fearless"?
bank.explanation: The suffix "-less" means without, so "fearless" means without fear.

bank.prompt: What does the Greek root "bio" (as in biology) mean?
bank.explanation: The Greek root "bio" means life; biology is the study of living things.

bank.prompt: What does the Latin root "spect" (as in inspect) mean?
bank.explanation: The Latin root "spect" means to look; to inspect means to look closely at something.

bank.prompt: The arid desert had no rain. What does "arid" mean?
bank.explanation: The context clue "no rain" tells the reader that "arid" means very dry.
